messages:
maria: Hey team — Acme (tenant=acme-platform) is hitting p95 spikes ~2.3s and intermittent 429s on their dedicated eu1 pool over the last ~45m. Customer reports sudden GPU util jumps and I see some CUDA errors in the app logs (sample req acme-req-98321). Can we triage?

alex: On it. Which pool id and node(s)? Any obvious packing info?

maria: pool=ded-eu1-142, node ids: host-42a, host-42b. I pasted the relevant snippet from their request logs below.

maria: ```
[2026-03-16T10:12:03Z] acme-req-98321 GENERATE start uid=...
[2026-03-16T10:12:03Z] gpu0 util=95% mem=83% latency=2300ms ERROR: CUDA error: launch failed
[2026-03-16T10:12:05Z] 429 returned to client
```

ben: Share ops-bot allocation dump for host-42a/42b, might show packing.

ops-bot: ```
host-42a: pool=ded-eu1-142 slices=[1g.10gb@slice0 tenant=acme-platform, 1g.5gb@slice1 tenant=other-tenant]
host-42b: pool=ded-eu1-142 slices=[1g.5gb@slice0 tenant=acme-platform, 1g.5gb@slice1 tenant=vendor-x]
```

alex: Hmm — acme has fractional slices on both hosts (1g.10gb + 1g.5gb). Small MIG partitions + co-residency can cause L3/cross-slice thrash and strange latency/429 patterns under bursty workloads. Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor / slice-level contention.

jordan: Also seeing KV cache heatmap for acme shows repeated full-cache evictions coinciding with the p95 spikes — likely warmup + eviction storms when other tenant bursts. L3/SM contention plausible.

maria: Customer is sensitive to cost, can't move to full GPU immediately. Can we repro in lab with their request pattern to confirm? They'll accept a temporary mitigation if it reduces 429s.

alex: Steps to repro in our lab: send a burst workload that matches their profile — many short requests (~40-100 tokens) at 120 rps for 30s. Example curl:```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ACME_TOKEN' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-xxl-8k","input":"Summarize X","max_tokens":80}'
```
Run with a few parallel clients to simulate co-resident bursts. If we see p95 spikes and 429s on fractional slices, we confirm contention.

ben: Short mitigation we can apply from control plane: adjust autoscale/packing hints to keep at least one free slice per host in the pool (min_free_slices=1) for ded-eu1-142 so acme's slices avoid being packed next to high-burst tenants. Applying now via admin API.

ops-bot: ```
POST /admin/pools/ded-eu1-142/config {"min_free_slices":1} -> 202 Accepted
Allocation rebalancer triggered for pool ded-eu1-142. Moving 1 slice to host-44c to create slack.```

maria: Policy applied — I'm seeing p95 drop to ~250ms on the next 10m, and the 429s stopped for the moment. Customer reports improved UX. :thumbsup:

jordan: Good short-term fix. Action items for next week: 1) reproduce in lab with parallel bursters and capture SM/L3 metrics, 2) audit MIG partitioning recommendations (re-evaluate 1g.5gb packing policy), 3) open ticket for driver/firmware check on hosts with repeated thrash. Tagging @platform-team for partitioning policy change.

alex: I'll log the repro run and attach perf traces. Also propose a rollout to default min_free_slices=1 for high-IO models until we finish analysis.

maria: Thanks all — Customer is aware it's a temporary control-plane mitigation and we suggested a billing-safe trial for reserved larger slices. I'll follow up with acme on next steps.

ben: Filing infra ticket INF-2026-789 for longer-term partitioning/packing tuning and host driver check.

alex: Summary: noisy neighbor on fractional MIG slices caused eviction/latency spikes -> applied min_free_slices mitigation -> immediate improvement. Next: lab repro + partitioning audit + driver ticket. Closing thread unless new spikes. :white_check_mark:
